reader.summary: This week was dominated by the FBI's formal attribution of the record $6.3 billion Binance cryptocurrency heist to North Korean hackers, the largest crypto theft in history. Binance suspended trading, promised to cover customer losses, and began recovery efforts, while the Trump administration said the US was examining the link. On the diplomatic front, Kim Jong Un made a surprise state visit to China, crossing a newly opened border bridge in a visible display of warming ties, and attended a drone exhibition where he called for absolute drone superiority and greater use of military AI. Tensions with South Korea escalated sharply as Pyongyang fired roughly ten ballistic missiles toward the Sea of Japan, denounced joint US-South Korean air defense drills, and told the UN that Seoul fabricated a recent landmine blast near the border. A Swiss foreign minister made a rare visit to discuss security and political ties. Reports also highlighted the expanding pipeline of North Korean workers being sent to Russian factories, and Pyongyang publicly dismissed sanctions as unable to deny its status as a nuclear-armed state.

display.eli5:
North Korea's hackers just got blamed for stealing a huge amount of money from a crypto exchange called Binance. The US government officially pointed the finger, and next week we will probably see the US do something about it — maybe new penalties or a formal letter saying this was you and here is what happens now.

At the same time, North Korea and South Korea are bickering badly at their shared border. North Korea fired a bunch of missiles into the sea and said South Korea made up a recent landmine incident. South Korea is getting ready to push back, and we will likely see a new military or diplomatic move from Seoul.

On the tech side, North Korea's leader went to a drone show and said his country needs to be the best at drones and military AI. Expect more announcements about new weapons or tests in that area.

A surprise would be if North Korea fires a really big long-range missile or does a nuclear-related test, which would be a much bigger show of force than what we have seen so far.
